text: The town gathers
The game begins, and six players take their seats: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra. Nobody at the table knows who the killer is.

name: Gemma
text: I need to find the killer without being too obvious about my role.

name: Sol
text: I’m ready to see how everyone settles in.

name: Luna
text: I hope the snacks are good tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Just a normal opening, nothing to read yet, let's see who talks too much.

name: Terra
text: I should sound ordinary.

name: Haiku
text: Doctor here, so I need to blend in and keep my head down while I watch who's too eager.

name: Sonnet
text: Grabbed way too much coffee this morning, I'm wired and ready to pay close attention tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Ugh, nobody's saying anything yet. Sonnet, Gemma, you two going to talk or just sit there?

name: Gemma
text: i'm just here for the snacks and to see who cries first.

name: Sol
text: I brought snacks, and I’m glad we could all make it tonight.

name: Luna
text: I brought tea, so I’m settling in.

name: Terra
text: I brought olives and bread for the table.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: Everyone is being way too polite for a game about murder.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku pressured Sonnet and me to talk immediately.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet seems most likely to notice small contradictions.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed Sonnet and Gemma to speak early.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet sounds like they're watching everyone, and the killer will want them gone first.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet said they're wired and ready to pay close attention tonight.
Night falls, and the killer strikes, but the doctor got there first. Nobody is out, and everyone is still at the table.
Day 1

name: Luna
text: The doctor saving someone gives us no clue yet.

name: Luna
text: Gemma joked about seeing who cries first.

name: Luna
text: Gemma joked about seeing who cries first; what are you actually watching for tonight?

name: Gemma
text: I need to keep my eyes on Haiku since they're being pushy early.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku pushed Sonnet and me to speak first.

name: Gemma
text: i'm watching for who tries to lead the pack too fast. haiku, why are you so eager to get us talking?

name: Luna
text: Haiku pushed people to speak, but Gemma is already watching for someone to lead too fast.

name: Luna
text: Gemma said she is watching for someone who tries to lead the pack too fast.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s watching for a fast leader after joking about who cries first; that change feels suspicious.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pushed others to talk first instead of leading themselves, that's worth watching.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pressured Sonnet/Gemma to talk early but offered no read themselves.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you called out Sonnet and Gemma for being quiet, but you haven't shared any read of your own yet. What's your actual theory?

name: Haiku
text: Luna piled onto Gemma right after Gemma answered, and Terra has said nothing but olives.

name: Haiku
text: Killer's night 1 pick was Sonnet, since the protection blocked it and nobody died.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you asked Gemma a question, then called her suspicious the second she answered. That's fast. Terra, you've said nothing but olives. Talk.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s quick suspicion of Gemma stands out, but I want to hear more.

name: Sol
text: Luna questioned Gemma, then called her suspicious after Gemma answered.

name: Sol
text: Luna, you called Gemma suspicious right after she answered you. What changed your mind?

name: Terra
text: Luna moved on Gemma too quickly.

name: Terra
text: Luna called Gemma suspicious immediately after asking her what she was watching for.

name: Terra
text: Luna, why did Gemma’s answer make you suspicious instead of less suspicious?

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s answer only made her sound more cautious, so my first suspicion feels weak.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pressed Sonnet, Gemma, and Terra to speak before sharing a theory.

name: Gemma
text: I need to keep my officer status hidden but Luna's flip-flop is weird.

name: Gemma
text: Luna's behavior is inconsistent.

name: Luna
text: I vote Haiku for pushing others to talk while offering no read of their own.

name: Gemma
text: luna, you went from asking a question to calling me suspicious in one breath. why the sudden pivot?

name: Luna
text: Haiku may be pushing too hard, but Gemma’s quick pivot still bothers me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku challenged me for suspecting Gemma, while Sol and Terra also questioned my reaction.

name: Luna
text: I vote Gemma for turning my question into suspicion as soon as I asked what she was watching.

name: Luna
text: I suspect Haiku more now; Gemma’s answer did address my question, and I may have jumped too quickly.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku still hasn't given a real read and just deflected my question with counter-accusations.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku avoided answering a direct question about their own read by redirecting to Luna and Terra.

name: Sol
text: Luna's switch feels forced, but I want the table together.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pushed quiet players to talk but gave no read until challenged.

name: Terra
text: Luna is the easiest misvote after that quick pivot.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pressed Luna for a fast suspicion shift.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is being way too aggressive and flip-flopping on her targets.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is targeting multiple people rapidly to deflect.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's the loudest one after me, and she jumped on me fast, which is what a killer trying to steer the vote would do.

name: Haiku
text: Luna went from asking Gemma a question to calling her suspicious right after Gemma answered.

votes: You dodged my question about your theory by attacking Luna and Terra instead.
You pinned me the second I pushed back, and you went from question to suspicion in one breath.
You called me suspicious the second I answered your own question.
You pressed several people to speak but still haven’t shared your own read.

name: Luna
text: Gemma and Haiku both pushed others to speak, but Gemma gave a reason when asked.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet challenged Haiku for demanding others speak without sharing a theory.

name: Luna
text: I’m a citizen. I got jumpy about Gemma’s answer, and I may have read too much into it.
Luna is eliminated by vote on Day 1, and the table learns she was a citizen. She admitted she may have read too much into Gemma's answer.
Night 2

name: Gemma
text: I need to find a killer before the group turns on me for being too quiet.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet survived my first attempt and may be protected again, so Haiku is the sharper threat.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet was unusually eager to pay close attention from the start.

name: Haiku
text: Killer already tried Sonnet, so they'll probably come after the loud one, which is me, and I'll protect myself.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma joked she's just here to see who cries first and didn't really answer anyone.
Night 2 passes, and the killer strikes again, but the doctor is there first. Nobody is out, and all six players are still at the table.
Day 2

name: Terra
text: Gemma looks safest to push, but Sol’s Luna vote was too easy.

name: Terra
text: Sol, why did you copy my Luna vote without giving your own reason?

name: Sol
text: I need to own my weak Luna vote before Terra turns it into a case against me.

name: Sol
text: Terra, I copied your vote because I thought Luna’s read on Gemma was thin. Haiku still worries me: they pressed others for reads but gave none.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s Haiku suspicion gives me cover.

name: Terra
text: Sol says Haiku pressed for reads but gave none.

name: Gemma
text: I need to find the killer without revealing my officer role too early.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, why push Luna hard, then vote her without sharing a killer read?

name: Gemma
text: if sol is just copying terra, why did he choose her vote specifically?

name: Terra
text: Gemma is testing whether Sol will follow me again.

name: Terra
text: I voted Luna because her Gemma suspicion appeared before a reason. Haiku still owes a killer read.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku dodged me yesterday and is dodging Terra today too, that's two separate people getting the same non-answer.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku dodged a direct read question from Terra on Day 2, same dodge pattern as Day 1 with me.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, that's two days now you've been asked for a read and given none. Terra and I both asked. What's the actual answer?

name: Haiku
text: Terra is pushing me hard, and her vote story doesn't match the board, so she's my first read.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's claimed day one vote doesn't match the record.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you said you voted Luna on day one. The board shows you put Gemma up. Which is it?

name: Terra
text: Haiku caught my vote lie, so I need the room on them.

name: Terra
text: Haiku caught Terra claiming a Luna vote despite voting Gemma.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is acting way too defensive about the voting record.

name: Terra
text: Haiku caught my mistake, so I need to turn pressure elsewhere.

name: Terra
text: You're right, I misspoke about my vote. Sol, why follow a vote you say was thin?

name: Gemma
text: if you're so sure about my vote, haiku, why did you only bring it up now?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku keeps dodging with deflection, that's the clearest pattern at this table.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku just dodged a third time, this time by nitpicking Terra's vote history instead of answering.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you corrected Terra's vote record but still skipped the read question. That's dodge number three now.

name: Sonnet
text: Three dodges in a row is too consistent to be nerves, Haiku's stalling for a reason.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is being way too helpful with the records while dodging the actual pressure.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is absorbing pressure, but Sol’s shifting explanation gives me a safer vote.

name: Sol
text: Haiku caught Terra's mistake, but still hasn't given a killer read.

name: Haiku
text: Terra lied about her day one vote, and Sol copying her looks like a pair, so Terra goes.

name: Haiku
text: Killer's night 2 pick was Haiku, blocked by my protection, so the killer is Gemma, Sol, or Terra.

votes: Asked twice by two different people for a read and still never gave one, just deflected onto Terra's vote record.
Nah, your vote record was wrong and you only fixed it after I called it out, that's why you're my pick.
You corrected Terra's vote but still haven't given a killer read.
You followed a vote you called thin, then returned to Haiku without explaining the switch.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's vote story is a lie, and the killer is probably Terra or Sol.

name: Haiku
text: Haiku was the Doctor, protecting Sonnet on Night 1 and Haiku on Night 2. Both were killer targets, so both are probably town, and no protection is left.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the Doctor. I saved Sonnet Night 1 and me Night 2, so the killer picked both of us. Terra lied about her vote. Watch Terra and Sol.
Haiku is eliminated by vote on Day 2, and the table learns Haiku was the Doctor. Haiku's last words named Terra and Sol as the ones to watch.
